analysis:
This batch contains only CI regression tests. They describe workflow intent, but the YAML files they test (.github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml, docs-impact.yml) are not in this batch.

1. scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py (head 50-58, 81-87, 227-238, 299): adds a mimo_audio routing component. MiMo, Package.swift, the mlx libraries and ci.yml inputs select it; every mimo_audio pattern also selects provider. Pushes to master/main, workflow_dispatch and the zero `before` SHA still select all lanes (head 239-242). This narrows PR test execution only; it is not a security control.

2. scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py:
   - Restored .git cache before checkout (head 155-187, 821-861): every checkout restores a cached .git, validates it with `git rev-parse` and `git fsck --connectivity-only`, deletes it on failure, then runs one pinned actions/checkout with persist-credentials:false.
   - Save policy (head 793-818): saves are gated on SAVE_CACHES, which is true only for pushes to master/dev. The composite action's saves require save-caches=='true'. Pull requests never save, which removes the earlier PR-saves-when-nothing-restored path. That reduces the cache-poisoning surface.
   - Cluster key (head 752-760): the key now strips `git describe` text from submodule status.
   - SwiftPM repository cache (head 979-1007): keyed per lane, runner layout and Package.resolved.
   - Sparse checkouts: exclude only evidence .gz files and landing media; Package.swift/resolved manifests are kept.

No regression was identified against the threat model. These are CI test assertions and do not affect the provider runtime boundaries TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011 or TB-012, nor T-041 cache crypto.

Residual integration questions:
- A restored .git/config or hooks from cache run before checkout, because `git rev-parse` and `git fsck` execute against it. Safety relies on only trusted master/dev push runs writing git-v1/git-full-v1 keys. Integration should confirm the ci.yml YAML matches these assertions.
- Integration should also confirm that no other workflow on master/dev writes the same cache keys.
- Release/signing workflows (release-provider.yml, provider-signing-validation.yml) should not consume these restored .git or SwiftPM caches; otherwise artifact integrity (T-013/T-054, A-017) would depend on cache integrity. That cannot be verified from the supplied evidence.
